params.body:
Four items from Frederik's walk-through on cutover day, one PR.

## 1. The UI-selected language wins everywhere (R P2-10.22)

A dealer with Dutch in his settings who switched to French in the header read French labels over Dutch values: transmission, fuel, body style, colour, paint, category, options and their values, option groups and portals came from `Auth::user()->language->shortcode` in the repository pluck (`DbRepository::languageColumn`), in `Enumeration::getOptionGroups` and in ten blades as `$lang = ...`, while `SetLangMiddleware` already put the header choice in the locale. The own-stock and Stocklist filter lists were hard-coded to `name_nl` in caches without a language in the key.

Shane's rule: the settings language is only the DEFAULT for the switch; once the user switches, everything follows the UI locale. One source, `Custom::lang()` (request locale, then settings language, then legacy session id, then nl), `getNameField()` on top; every caller routed through it. Cached lists carry the locale in their key (`sl_fuel_fr`, `ownstock_filter_options_name_fr`, ...), `WarmCaches` expects the new keys. The website iframe keeps its `lang` parameter; mails stay in the recipient's language.

Behaviour change, decided by Shane: finding `2026-09-15-namen-volgden-de-instellingentaal-niet-het-scherm.md` (opgelost). Two existing tests that pinned "settings language decides" now set the screen locale.

## 2. The sheet keeps its step on refresh (R S1-9.21)

`initialStep()` read `?tab=` but nothing wrote it back, so a refresh on Foto's returned to Algemeen. The Alpine root now watches `tab` and writes `?tab=<step>` with `history.replaceState` (no history entry per step; Back still leaves the sheet). Sits next to the scroll-to-top from PR 438.

## 3. French leftovers

"Niet gepubliceerd" and "Concept" chips on the sheet header, the "Status" label, the step counter ("Stap 2 van 8"), the "Beheer" dropdown, the section titles of the general step (Voertuiggegevens, Belastingen, Garantie, Locatie, Beschrijving, "Beschrijving stocklist"), "Handelsprijs invullen" on the row, "Openen" and "Weergave" on the settings tabs; all through `ui.*` keys in nl/fr/en/de. The ui keys that only existed in Dutch (footer links, show more, showing count, search relations) now exist in fr and de, and `showing_count` had its nl and en values swapped. `FrenchLeftoversTest` renders the sheet and the settings tabs as a French user and asserts none of the Dutch strings; it also checks every `ui` key exists in the four languages.

## 4. Own-fleet description in four languages, with Translate with AI (R S1-4.8)

Settings > AI: the fixed text is now a tab strip nl/fr/en/de with one textarea each, stored as `ai_own_text_<lang>` (short on purpose: `settings.key` is varchar(30) and the old key `ai_dealer_own_commercial_text_` is exactly 30 characters, so `..._nl` would be truncated onto the old key). The old row is read as Dutch until the form is saved once (no migration). "Vertalen met AI" posts the text of the open tab to `settings.ai.translate` -> `VehicleTextService::translate` (same client, key and `Outbound::allows('openai')` gate as the sales text) and fills the other three in the form; a filled language is only overwritten after `ui.confirm`; nothing is saved until Opslaan. `VehicleObserver::creating` takes the dealer's language, Dutch when empty, else the first filled language. Alpine component `ownFleetText` lives in `layouts/app.blade.php`.

Open point: translating the other AI fields (company info, prompt) the same way later.

## Tests

`UiLocaleTest`, `OwnFleetTextTest`, `FrenchLeftoversTest`, `VehicleFormStepTest::test_the_sheet_keeps_its_step_in_the_url`; adapted `WarmCachesTest`, `StocklistBrowserTest`, `VehicleSheetOptionOrderTest`, `SettingsSayWhatTheyAreTest`. Filter run (Lang|Locale|Translation|VehicleForm|Settings|Stocklist|OpenAI|RulesCoverage|RulesIdentity|CompiledViews|AlpineExpression|HandlerWiring|StylesheetSyntax|WarmCaches): 220 tests green.

Screenshot: `.playwright-mcp/ui-locale/ai-tab-1440.png` (AI tab, Dutch tab open, Frans/Engels/Duits marked leeg, Translate button under the field).
params.title: The UI language wins everywhere, the sheet keeps its step on refresh, and the fleet description speaks four languages
